items.note: Stem asked which actions 'reduce the risk of falls' but keyed 'encourage participation in therapy and self-care', which the book lists as independent care, not fall prevention; stem broadened to the plan of care so every key is supported by p.144.

Distractor 'High vitamin D levels' sat beside the key 'Low vitamin D levels', an opposite pair that gave one answer away; replaced with hypertension and added a sixth unkeyed option (regular exercise).
Stem referred to 'the book' rather than presenting a client scenario; reworded as a client-centered item.

Sudden unilateral facial weakness is a stroke warning sign, so the thrombolytic distractor was not defensibly wrong; stem now states stroke was ruled out and the rt-PA distractor was replaced with IVIG/plasmapheresis (GBS).
